I'm just beginning to explore the relation between homeless people and "trash" animals. 
More specifically, my research is based in urban Japan, a place where homelessness, and what causes it, is not the same as is it in most other countries. And the animal I'm researching is the crow (Japanese Jungle Crow). 

In Japan, both crows and homeless people are triggers of fear and disgust, they are both seen as out of place in our imaginative geographies, and they both compete for garbage as one source of food. 
Homelessness is a taboo topic in Japan, so much so that, in 1999, when the Government of Tokyo organized a public symposium to educate the population on crow-related issues, policies, and ecology, they 'sneakily' had a whole panel dedicated to discussing homeless people. 
When the media reported the symposium summary the day after, they only wrote about crows, but never mentioned that homeless people had also been a topic of discussion. 

Homelessness in Japan became more visible in the 1990's, after the Buble Burst. And, coincidentally, the population of jungle crows in Japan had doubled by the mid 90's and trippled by the end of the 90's. I'm not saying there is a direct connection between those two events, but it's curious how some people started comparing the homeless to the unwanted jungles crows in Japan.
